after.claim: (Preparation.) Since $b_k\to b\in(0,\infty]$ in the cases below, for every fixed $T<b$ the interval $[0,T]$ is contained in $[0,b_k]$ for all large $k$, and for the past side $[-T,0]\subseteq[-b_k,0]$ for all large $k$. We work with subsequences obtained by the diagonal procedure of [L1] and do not relabel beyond that.

(Imprisonment.) Assume $(M,g,N)$ strongly causal and $\alpha_k([0,b_k])\subseteq K$ with $K$ compact. By [L5], $\ell_h(\alpha_k)\le L(K)$ for every $k$; since the curves are $h$-arclength-parametrized, $b_k=\ell_h(\alpha_k)\le L(K)$, so $b=\lim_kb_k\le L(K)<\infty$.

(Limit on compact subintervals of $[0,b)$.) Apply [L1] clause (a) successively on $[0,b-1/n]$ for $n$ with $b-1/n>0$ and diagonalize over $n$: there is a subsequence, still written $\alpha_k$, and a future causal curve $\alpha:[0,b)\to M$ with $\alpha(0)=x$, $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le t-s$, such that $\alpha_k\to\alpha$ uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of $[0,b)$.

(The future tail.) By step 1.1 and [L1] clause (b) applied to the curves $\alpha_k$ restricted to $[0,n]$ and diagonalized over $n$, there are a subsequence and a future-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$ such that $\alpha_k\to\alpha^+$ uniformly in $d_h$ on every compact subinterval of $[0,\infty)$.

(The past tail.) Define $\delta_k(s):=\alpha_k(b_k+s)$ for $s\in[-b_k,0]$; then $\delta_k$ is a future causal curve parametrized by $h$-arclength with $\delta_k(0)=\alpha_k(b_k)\to z$ and $[-n,0]\subseteq[-b_k,0]$ for all large $k$. Applying the dual of [L1] clause (b) (in the time-reversed orientation) and diagonalizing over $n$, we obtain a subsequence and a future causal curve $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with $\alpha^-(0)=z$, past-inextendible, such that $\delta_k\to\alpha^-$ uniformly on compact subintervals of $(-\infty,0]$. Choosing the subsequence simultaneously for $\alpha^+$ and $\alpha^-$ (a nested subsequence) gives (ii) up to the closure relation.

(Extension to the endpoint $b$.) Define $\alpha(b):=z$. For $s<b$ and $t\in(s,b)$, $d_h(\alpha(s),\alpha(t))\le t-s$ by step 2.1; letting $t\uparrow b$ and using $d_h(\alpha(t),z)\to0$ (which follows from $d_h(\alpha(t),z)\le d_h(\alpha(t),\alpha_k(t))+d_h(\alpha_k(t),\alpha_k(b_k))+d_h(\alpha_k(b_k),z)$ with uniform convergence on $[s,b-1/n]$ and $b_k\to b$) gives $d_h(\alpha(s),z)\le b-s$. Hence the extended $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ is $1$-Lipschitz for $d_h$, in particular locally Lipschitz in charts, locally absolutely continuous, and a future causal curve on $[0,b]$: on $[0,b)$ it has the almost-everywhere future causal derivative of step 2.1, and the single endpoint contributes a null set.

(The closure relation.) Fix $t_+\ge0$ and $t_-\le0$. Since $b_k\to\infty$, for all $k\ge k_0$ we have $t_+\le b_k+t_-$, so both parameter values lie in the domain $[0,b_k]$ with $t_+\le b_k+t_-$. By [L2], $\alpha_k(t_+)\le\alpha_k(b_k+t_-)=\delta_k(t_-)$. Passing to the limit along the chosen subsequence, $u_k:=\alpha_k(t_+)\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ (step 2.2) and $v_k:=\delta_k(t_-)\to\alpha^-(t_-)$ (step 2.3), with $u_k\le v_k$ for all large $k$. This is the closure statement of (ii).

(Uniform convergence on $[0,b]$.) Let $\varepsilon>0$ and choose $T<b$ with $b-T<\varepsilon/4$. On $[0,T]$ we have uniform convergence by step 2.1. For $t\in[T,b]$ and large $k$: $$d_h(\alpha_k(t),\alpha(t))\le d_h(\alpha_k(t),\alpha_k(b_k))+d_h(\alpha_k(b_k),z)+d_h(z,\alpha(t))\le (b_k-t)+(b_k-t)+o(1)<\varepsilon,$$ using the Lipschitz bounds $d_h(\alpha_k(t),\alpha_k(b_k))\le b_k-t$ and $d_h(\alpha(t),z)\le b-t$, and $b_k\to b$. Hence $\alpha_k\to\alpha$ uniformly on $[0,b]$. This proves (i) for $b>0$.

(The case $b=0$.) If $b=0$, then for each $k$, $$d_h(x,z)\le d_h(x,\alpha_k(0))+d_h(\alpha_k(0),\alpha_k(b_k))+d_h(\alpha_k(b_k),z)\le o(1)+b_k+o(1)\to0,$$ so $x=z$; and $\sup_{t\in[0,b_k]}d_h(\alpha_k(t),x)\le d_h(\alpha_k(0),x)+b_k\to0$, so the curves converge uniformly to the constant curve at $x$ on the (shrinking) domains, giving (i) with $b=0$ and the constant curve.

(Coincident endpoints in the unbounded case.) If $x=z$, the concatenation $\gamma:\mathbb R\to M$, $\gamma(t):=\alpha^-(t)$ for $t\le0$ and $\gamma(t):=\alpha^+(t)$ for $t\ge0$, is a future causal curve by [L3] (both pieces are future causal and meet at $x=z$); it is past-inextendible because $\alpha^-$ is, and future-inextendible because $\alpha^+$ is, hence inextendible. This is the second half of (iii); the first half follows from (i) with $b>0$: $\alpha(0)=\alpha(b)=x$ and $\alpha$ is nonconstant on $[0,b]$ by [L1] (a4), so it is a nonconstant closed future causal curve.
